dedupe_keys.name: enisa inter x study of the resilience of the internet interconnection ecosystem 2010 to 2011

description: This risk assessment and policy case is ENISA's study of how resilient the system of interconnection between internet networks is, and what policy makers could do about it. Launched in 2010, the study consulted a large number of network operators, exchanges and experts and was published in early 2011 as the report Inter-X: Resilience of the Internet Interconnection Ecosystem, with an abridged paper by Chris Hall, Ross Anderson, Richard Clayton, Evangelos Ouzounis and Panagiotis Trimintzios. It set out scenarios for systemic failure, such as a regional loss of power or of the people needed to run networks, cascading technical failures, and coordinated attacks that inject bogus routes, and found evidence that some BGP implementations are fragile, that some concentrations of infrastructure lack resilience, and that the health of the system as a whole is nobody's priority. It highlighted a striking lack of information about the size and shape of the infrastructure and the risk of a tragedy of the commons, and recommended independent investigation of major incidents, research on inter-domain routing and traffic prioritisation in a crisis, better routing security and exercises. Coverage: the European and global interconnection system around 2010. Format and access: report PDF from ENISA and an open preprint of the paper, free. Caveats: qualitative; ENISA's site refused automated access, so details come from the paper. Simulation uses: scenarios for cascading failure and hazard exposure of interconnection, and policy analysis of routing security. Related records: the DE-CIX and AMS-IX outages and the Rostelecom hijack illustrate its scenarios.
